item.title: Stepwise transitions unlock three spin states and diverse SHG in a polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex
item.description:
Ying-Ying Wu, Zi-Yi Zhang, Shu-Qi Wu, Ryuta Ishikawa, Akio Mishima, Zi-Han Yan, Guang-Yan Xu, Jing-Wei Dai, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78097-5
Abstract Multifunctional spin-crossover materials are promising for information storage and nonlinear optics, yet stepwise spin-crossover coupled with controllable second harmonic generation switching is hindered by poor thermal stability of non-centrosymmetric lattices. Herein, we report an air-stable polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex displaying cooling-induced two-step spin-crossover but one-step transition during heating, delivering a wide thermal hysteresis of 75 K (199 K cooling / 274 K heating) via intense intermolecular cooperativity. Sequential phase evolution ( P 1 → P 1 → Pn ) creates three discrete spin configurations with c -axis cell duplication followed by a symmetry-increasing transition to full low-spin phase upon cooling. Second harmonic generation tests verify three separable nonlinear optical states consistent with magnetic responses. Crystal stacking analysis and density functional theory calculations validate that spin ordering-phase transition synergy rearranges molecular dipoles to realize stepwise second harmonic generation modulation. This study offers an original route toward dual spin-optic functional materials for optical storage applications.

item.title: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation of mediodorsal thalamus disrupts decision flexibility during reward learning
item.description:
Graeme Mackenzie, William Gilmour, Isla Barnard, Shen-Shen Yang, Szabolcs Suveges, Jennifer MacFarlane, Avinash Kanodia, James Manfield, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79431-7
Abstract When learning to find the most beneficial course of action, the prefrontal cortex guides decisions by comparing estimates of the relative value of the options available. Basic neuroscience studies in animals support the view that the thalamus can regulate this activity within and across the prefrontal cortex. We studied a group of patients (n = 37) undergoing unilateral MR-guided focused ultrasound for essential tremor, performing the restless bandit, a reward reinforcement learning task, immediately before and after thalamotomy. Thalamotomy significantly impaired the proportion of switch choices during the task without affecting overall performance. This effect was observed when the task was delivered to co-incide with maximal vasogenic thalamic oedema but not in a control group tested on the same day of their treatment. A reinforcement learning model fitted to the patients’ choices replicated the effect of thalamotomy when the model increased exploitation of the bandits’ learnt value estimate. This shift in the explore-exploit trade-off, manifesting as reduced choice flexibility, co-varied with the pattern of post-operative oedema extension into the mediodorsal nucleus. These findings confirm a causal role of the thalamus and specifically the mediodorsal nucleus in regulating the extent to which value estimates are used to guide decisions and learning from reward.
